# Container

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Wraps one child with optional sizing, alignment, padding, borders, background, and layers.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`. Extends `BorderedElementBase`. Implements `IContentContainer`, `IStatefulElement`.

## Constructors

```typescript
new Container()
new Container(options: ContainerOptions)
```

### `clipContent`

```typescript
clipContent: boolean
```

When `true` and [`BorderedElementBase.cornerRadius`](bordered-element-base.md#cornerradius) is positive, the container's content (background, border, and child) is clipped to the rounded-rectangle outline. This is what turns a rounded background into a true rounded-corner card: a full-bleed image or any overflowing child is masked to the rounded box rather than spilling past the corners. Defaults to `false`, so setting `cornerRadius` alone keeps the historical behaviour of a rounded fill/stroke with un-clipped content.

Example, from `industry-templates/compliance-audit/audit-report`:

```typescript
c.clipContent = true;
```

Example, from `industry-templates/field-service-property/inventory-schedule-of-condition`:

```typescript
box.clipContent = true;
```

### `crispEdges`

```typescript
crispEdges: boolean
```

When `true`, the container's subtree renders inside a crisp-edge region: on SVG page export it emits `<g shape-rendering="crispEdges">`, so thin axis-aligned strokes and rectangles (grid/table lines, dividers) snap to the device pixel grid instead of being antialiased into a soft blur. It is a no-op on PDF output (the bytes are unchanged; crispness there is the viewer's job). Only wrap axis-aligned content — rounded rects, circles, diagonals, and text want antialiasing and will look jagged inside a crisp-edge region.

### `fillHeight`

```typescript
fillHeight: boolean
```

When `true`, the container takes the body content height left on the current page instead of sizing to its content. This is the primitive behind the header / body / footer page shape: the middle band is whatever the page chrome leaves over, a figure an author cannot compute up front because both templates are functions of the page number.

`height` wins outright — fill is only consulted when no height is pinned — and fill never *shrinks* content: a container whose child is taller than the space left keeps the child's height and paginates normally. Measurement is unaffected (it reports the natural content height, because a pure measure has no cursor to measure from); only arrangement expands.

Combines with `verticalAlignment`: the slack fill creates is exactly the space it gained, so `'bottom'` anchors content to the foot of the band.

Example, from `code-recipes/getting-started/simple-document`:

```typescript
card.fillHeight = true;
```

### `horizontalAlignment`

```typescript
horizontalAlignment: HorizontalAlignment | undefined
```

Horizontal alignment of the child within the container's available width. When the child is narrower than the container, it is positioned accordingly; otherwise it fills the width as before. `undefined`/`Start` keep the default left placement. `Stretch` is treated as "fill" (no offset).

Accepts `'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch'` on write.

Example, from `industry-templates/finance-reporting/financial-dashboard`:

```typescript
container6.horizontalAlignment = 'center';
```

Example, from `industry-templates/education-public-sector/uk-degree-transcript`:

```typescript
qrWrap.horizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.End;
```

### `padding`

```typescript
padding: Thickness
```

Padding inside the container, inside the border.

Accepts `12`, `[h, v]`, `[l, t, r, b]` or `{ bottom: 12 }` on write ; omitted sides are zero.

Example, from `industry-templates/finance-reporting/financial-dashboard`:

```typescript
container10.padding = 4;
```

Example, from `industry-templates/finance-reporting/financial-dashboard`:

```typescript
container17.padding = 12;
```

### `verticalAlignment`

```typescript
verticalAlignment: VerticalAlignment | undefined
```

Vertical alignment of the child within the container's available height. Only has an effect when the container is taller than its child needs - normally because `height` is set - so it is the way to anchor content to the bottom (or middle) of a fixed box without hand-computing a top padding against a font's metrics. `undefined`/`Start` keep the default top placement; `Stretch` is treated as "fill" (no offset).

Accepts `'top' | 'middle' | 'bottom' | 'stretch'` on write.

Example, from `industry-templates/finance-reporting/financial-dashboard`:

```typescript
container5.verticalAlignment = 'middle';
```

Example, from `industry-templates/finance-reporting/financial-dashboard`:

```typescript
container6.verticalAlignment = 'middle';
```

## Methods

- [`getChildren`](#getchildren): Canonical child traversal for engine tree walks (the default-style cascade, font/image discovery).
- [`layers`](#layers): Fills this container with an inline z-stack.
- [`renderStateful`](#renderstateful): Renders this element with state tracking for pagination.
- [`resetState`](#resetstate): Resets the internal state of this element, preparing it for a fresh render.

### `getChildren`

```typescript
getChildren(): readonly IElement[]
```

Canonical child traversal for engine tree walks (the default-style cascade, font/image discovery). Container elements return their direct renderable children; leaf elements omit it. Optional so existing custom IElement implementations remain source-compatible.

### `layers`

```typescript
layers(configure: (layers: LayersDescriptor) => void): Container
```

Fills this container with an inline z-stack. Layers paint in declaration order: `background` behind, `primaryLayer` in the middle (it sets the flow height), and `foreground` on top.

```typescript
new Container().layers(layers => layers
  .background(Image.load('card-bg.jpg'))
  .foreground(new TextBlock('Sample Company')));
```

### `renderStateful`

```typescript
renderStateful(ctx: RenderContext, width: number): RenderStatus
```

Renders this element with state tracking for pagination. Unlike Render(), this method returns a status indicating whether more content needs to be rendered on subsequent pages.

- `ctx`: The render context
- `width`: The available width for this element

### `resetState`

```typescript
resetState(): void
```

Resets the internal state of this element, preparing it for a fresh render. Should be called before starting a new document or after completing a multipage render.
